# Supply network extraction

## Task

You will receive a document that describes one supply network: its planning periods, its products, its nodes (suppliers, plants, distribution centres and customers), the lanes that ship goods between nodes, and each node's demand or inventory. Turn it into the five CSV files below, which the SNRM supply-network tool imports. Fill every cell from what the document states, or by the conventions below; never convert a unit and never invent a value.

<!-- schema: generated by netbench schema --format markdown; do not edit -->
## Files and columns

Five CSV files, comma-separated. Each starts with a header row naming every column of the file below, lower-case, in the order shown; every further row is one record. `*` marks a column SNRM requires; any other cell may be left blank. A number is plain digits with an optional `.` fraction (`1200`, `0.05`): no thousands separators, and no units or other text in the cell.

### network_meta.csv

| Column | Required | Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `period_length_value` | * | number | length of one simulation period, in period_length_unit |
| `period_length_unit` | * | time unit | unit of the period length |
| `horizon_periods` | * | number | number of periods simulated |
| `rounding_policy` |  | rounding policy | how durations round to whole periods; default NEAREST |
| `name` |  | text | the network's own name |

### nodes.csv

| Column | Required | Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | * | text | unique node name |
| `type` | * | node type | SUPPLIER, PLANT, DC or CUSTOMER |
| `capacity_value` |  | number | rate: units per capacity_time_unit; blank = uncapped |
| `capacity_time_unit` |  | time unit | denominator of capacity_value |
| `processing_time_value` |  | number | duration in processing_time_unit |
| `processing_time_unit` |  | time unit | unit of processing_time_value |
| `fixed_cost` |  | number | cost per period |
| `var_cost` |  | number | cost per unit |
| `failure_prob` |  | number | probability in [0, 1] |
| `region` |  | text | region tag |
| `lat` |  | number | latitude in degrees |
| `lng` |  | number | longitude in degrees |
| `pos_x` |  | number | editor canvas x (not geography) |
| `pos_y` |  | number | editor canvas y (not geography) |
| `caption` |  | text | annotation drawn under the name |
| `caption_visible` |  | true/false | true/false; blank = visible |

| Column | Required | Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `node` | * | text | node name |
| `product` | * | text | product name |

### Node types

`type` is one of:

| Value | Echelon rank |
|---|---|
| `SUPPLIER` | 0 |
| `PLANT` | 1 |
| `DC` | 2 |
| `CUSTOMER` | 3 |

### Time units

A `*_unit` cell holds one of these units, written as its name or as any of its tokens (case-insensitive):

| Unit | Seconds | Tokens |
|---|---|---|
| `SECOND` | 1 | `s`, `sec`, `secs`, `second`, `seconds` |
| `MINUTE` | 60 | `min`, `mins`, `minute`, `minutes` |
| `HOUR` | 3600 | `h`, `hr`, `hrs`, `hour`, `hours` |
| `DAY` | 86400 | `d`, `day`, `days` |
| `WEEK` | 604800 (7 days) | `wk`, `wks`, `week`, `weeks` |
| `MONTH` | 2592000 (30 days) | `mo`, `mon`, `month`, `months` |
| `YEAR` | 31536000 (365 days) | `y`, `yr`, `yrs`, `year`, `years` |

### Rounding policies

`rounding_policy` is one of:

| Value | Durations are rounded | 1.25 periods become | 1.5 periods become |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NEAREST` | to the nearest period | 1 | 2 |
| `UP` | up to the next whole period | 2 | 2 |
| `DOWN` | down to the previous whole period | 1 | 1 |

### Units

- Durations (the value is a length of time, measured in its unit):
  - network_meta.csv: `period_length_value` in `period_length_unit`
  - nodes.csv: `processing_time_value` in `processing_time_unit`
  - links.csv: `lead_time_value` in `lead_time_unit`
- Rates (the unit is the time denominator: so many per one unit of time):
  - nodes.csv: `capacity_value` per `capacity_time_unit`
  - links.csv: `capacity_value` per `capacity_time_unit`
  - node_products.csv: `demand_value` per `demand_time_unit`
  - node_products.csv: `holding_cost_value` per `holding_cost_time_unit`
- A missing or blank `*_unit` column or cell means the period unit (`period_length_unit`).
- A blank `capacity_value` (nodes.csv, links.csv) means uncapped.

### Conventions

Cells fixed by rule for the type of the row's node; a description never states them:

| Node type | File | Column | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CUSTOMER` | nodes.csv | `capacity_value` | blank |
| `CUSTOMER` | nodes.csv | `processing_time_value` | `0` |
| `CUSTOMER` | nodes.csv | `fixed_cost` | `0` |
| `CUSTOMER` | nodes.csv | `var_cost` | `0` |
| `CUSTOMER` | nodes.csv | `failure_prob` | `0` |
| `SUPPLIER`, `PLANT`, `DC` | node_products.csv | `demand_value` | `0` |
| `CUSTOMER` | node_products.csv | `initial_inventory` | `0` |
| `CUSTOMER` | node_products.csv | `safety_stock` | `0` |
| `CUSTOMER` | node_products.csv | `holding_cost_value` | `0` |

`0` may also be left blank. The unit cell next to a convention value holds the period unit (`period_length_unit`).
<!-- /schema -->

## Node types

A node's role in the document decides its `type`:

| Role in the document | `type` |
|---|---|
| supplier, tier-1 supplier, tier-2 supplier | `SUPPLIER` |
| plant, component plant, assembly plant | `PLANT` |
| distribution centre, central distribution centre, regional distribution centre | `DC` |
| customer | `CUSTOMER` |

Central and regional distribution centres are both `DC`; component and assembly plants are both `PLANT`; tier-1 and tier-2 suppliers are both `SUPPLIER`.

## Rows and conventions

- `network_meta.csv`: one row: the period length and its unit, the horizon in periods, the rounding policy (the value whose phrase the document uses) and the network's name.
- `nodes.csv`: one row per node. A customer's capacity is blank (uncapped) and its processing time, fixed cost, variable cost and failure probability are `0`.
- `links.csv`: one row per lane; `source` is the node that ships, `target` the node that receives.
- `products.csv`: one row per product.
- `node_products.csv`:
  - a customer has one row per product it demands, with that demand; its initial inventory, safety stock and holding cost are `0`.
  - a supplier, plant or distribution centre has one row per product it holds, with its initial inventory, safety stock and holding cost; its demand is `0` (or blank).
- These convention cells (the Conventions table above) are filled even though the document never states them; the unit cell next to one holds the period unit.

## Units

- Write every duration and rate in the unit the document states it in: "a lead time of 3 weeks" is `3` with `WEEK`, never `21` with `DAY`; "80 units per week" is `80` with `WEEK`.
- Whenever you fill a value that has a `*_unit` column, fill that unit column too, with the unit's upper-case name.
- A value the document does not state stays blank: leave both the value and its unit empty, never a guess or a default. A value stated as the same as another's ("the same safety stock as X") is stated: write that value.
- If the document gives a lane's distance in km and the lanes' speeds instead of the lane's lead time, the lead time is the distance divided by the speed of that lane's kind (road or ocean). Compute it in hours — distance ÷ speed per day × 24 — and write it with the unit `HOUR`.

## Numbers

Write every number in the CSV as plain digits, with a point as the decimal mark and no thousands separators, whatever the document uses: when the document says it groups digits (for example "Numbers use a point as the thousands separator and a comma as the decimal mark"), read its numbers that way and write `1.500` as `1500` and `2,75` as `2.75`.

## Names

Copy every name exactly as written (nodes, products, regions and the network), with the same spelling, capitals, spaces, hyphens and digits.

## Scope

Include only what the document states about the current network. Ignore historical, proposed, planned, discontinued or competitor information, even when it names real nodes or gives values.

## Response

Return exactly five fenced `csv` blocks, each preceded by a level-3 heading naming the file, in this order: `network_meta.csv`, `nodes.csv`, `links.csv`, `products.csv`, `node_products.csv`; no other text.
